blocks.text: A2-13 · Related pronouns
Lesson overview

The man who wears the glasses is the one who lost the bag, the colleague with whom I work.The person who arrives late signs the register.Then you describe people and things without repeating the name. In Arabic the relative pronoun ( ⁧الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الَّذِينَ⁩ ...) is used only after a given name and agrees with him; Inside its, when the name is not the subject, a pronoun of recovery recalls it ( ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ , letter. The book that I read it. After an indeterminate name its is not: ⁧كِتَابٌ قَرَأْتُهُ⁩ It's a book I read. Completing the Unit ⁧مَنْ⁩ ... ⁧مَا⁩ It's what it is. The context is the description of people and objects (announcements of lost property) and then work in an office. Two weeks.

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-13), script for speech synthesis, photos of people to describe, session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. Choose the right relative pronoun by gender and number (recognizing duals and plural female);
2. use the resume pronoun as an object complement, after a preposition and to say "whose" is;
3. build its without pronoun after an indeterminate name;
4. use ⁧مَنْ⁩ • who, the one who is ⁧مَا⁩ • what it is, including ⁧كُلُّ مَا⁩ • all that is done;
5. describe people and objects, understand a lost object ad and the rules of an office.
Texts. Dialogues and examples are given; the readings of the module A2.3 are partially vocalized (vowels on new words and where reading is ambiguous). Two-week plan.

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧المَرْأَةُ الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الشَّابَّانِ اللَّذَانِ⁩ : the relative pronoun follows a definite noun and agrees with it. The subject is not repeated in the relative ( ⁧الَّذِي يَلْبَسُ⁩ ), but the complement yes, with a suffix: ⁧الطَّالِبَانِ اللَّذَانِ دَعَاهُمَا بَاوْلُو⁩ □ the two students Paul invited (Lett. who invited them) ⁧السَّيِّدَةُ الَّتِي سَلَّمْتِ عَلَيْهَا⁩ The lady you greeted (Lett. on her) ⁧الحَلَوِيَّاتُ الَّتِي عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ⁩ : its can be without verb. ⁧كُلُّ مَنْ⁩ • all those who are entitled, ⁧مَنْ لَا يَعْرِفُهَا⁩ (section) 5). ⁧رُبَّمَا⁩ Maybe it is. ⁧حَلَوِيَّات⁩ Sweets. In this scene Umm Karīm is the neighbour of Salmā in Cairo, known in ONO-01: no connection with the colleague Karīm.
2. Related pronouns
1. Agreement. Its name takes the genre and number to which it refers: ⁧الوَلَدُ الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧البِنْتُ الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الطُّلَّابُ الَّذِينَ⁩ .
2. Plural of Things = ⁧الَّتِي⁩ . As with adjectives (A2-08): ⁧الكُتُبُ الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧السَّيَّارَاتُ الَّتِي⁩ .
3. The dual has two forms, such as the name: ⁧اللَّذَانِ⁩ the name, ⁧اللَّذَيْنِ⁩ to the parent and the accusative ( ⁧رَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَيْنِ⁩
⁧اللَّذَيْنِ⁩ …). The other forms do not decline.
4. The Plural Female ⁧اللَّوَاتِي⁩ / ⁧اللَّاتِي⁩ meets in the formal texts; many use ⁧الَّتِي⁩ also for women at Plural. Recognize him; Writing is okay too ⁧الَّتِي⁩ .
5. Graffia. ⁧الَّذِي⁩ , ⁧الَّتِي⁩ , ⁧الَّذِينَ⁩ they are written with only one lam and shadda; the duals and ⁧اللَّوَاتِي⁩ with two lam .

Only after a given name. Its Arabic is actually an adjective with the article: it is used when the name has the article, a suffix or is a proper name ( ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي⁩ …, ⁧كِتَابِي الَّذِي⁩ …, ⁧سَلْمَى الَّتِي⁩ …). After an indeterminate name it is not used (section 4). Unnamed. Its may be by itself: ⁧الَّذِي يَعْمَلُ هُنَا⁩ "The one who works here" ⁧هِيَ الَّتِي طَبَخَتْ⁩ She's the one who cooked. It's the Arabic way of saying "it's him who..." she's the one who...

blocks.text: Four comments:
1. The verb of its accords with its subject, which is not necessarily the starting name: ⁧الكُتُبُ الَّتِي⁩
⁧اشْتَرَاهَا أَبِي⁩ The books that my father bought (the subject is ⁧أَبِي⁩ ).
2. The subject-matter of the recovery is sometimes omitted in the formal writing ( ⁧الكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُ⁩ ). You always wear it.

3. Place and time. Where and when the relevant information is made by: ⁧فِيهِ⁩ / ⁧فِيهَا⁩ : ⁧المَدِينَةُ الَّتِي وُلِدْتُ فِيهَا⁩ The city in which I was born in New York, ⁧اليَوْمُ الَّذِي وَصَلْنَا فِيهِ⁩ The day we arrived.

4. Verbs with preposition (A2-10): the preposition remains in the relative with the suffix: ⁧الرَّقْمُ الَّذِي اتَّصَلْتُ بِهِ⁩ On number I called, ⁧الشَّخْصُ الَّذِي أَبْحَثُ عَنْهُ⁩ The person I'm looking for.
4. Its after an indeterminate name
After an indeterminate name its follows the name without relative pronoun, as an adjective. The recovery stays.

It is a very frequent construction in ads and news: ⁧مَطْلُوبٌ مُتَرْجِمٌ يَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ⁩ • Seek interpreter who speaks Arabic • ⁧رَأَيْتُ امْرَأَةً تَبْكِي⁩ I saw a woman crying. The first clue that tells you here begins a relative ' is an indeterminate name followed by a verb immediately. Watch your senses. A frequent mistake is to put ⁧الَّذِي⁩ after an indefinite name ( ⁧رَجُلٌ الَّذِي⁩ ...): it's wrong. And a phrase like ⁧عِنْدِي صَدِيقٌ يَسْكُنُ فِي رُومَا⁩ means "I have a friend who lives in Rome."He doesn't have a friend, he lives in Rome.

3. With prepositions ⁧مَنْ⁩ and ⁧مَا⁩ they melt: ⁧مِنْ⁩ + ⁧مَا⁩ → ⁧مِمَّا⁩ From what it does, ⁧عَنْ⁩ + ⁧مَا⁩ → ⁧عَمَّا⁩ • of what it is that it does, ⁧مِنْ⁩ + ⁧مَنْ⁩ →
⁧مِمَّنْ⁩ "Who's "Who': ⁧سَأَلَنِي عَمَّا حَدَثَ⁩ He asked me what happened. To be recognized.

allaḏī, allatī. The l is double and the ḏ of ⁧الَّذِي⁩ is sound interdental, like the English this: al-la-ḏī. After a word the alif falls: ⁧الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي⁩ = ar-raǧulu llaḏī. One melody. Name + relative + relative are said without pause: ar-raǧulu llaḏī yalbasu l-qamīṣ..., not raǧul… allaḏī…». The filming. The suffixes of the recovery must be clearly stated: qaraʾtuhu, fīhi, maʿahā.
